definitions.explanation: A category of household waste that can be incinerated, as defined by municipal garbage collection systems in Japan. Includes paper, food scraps, and certain plastics.

examples.japanese: {燃|も}えるゴミの{日|ひ}は{火曜日|かようび}だ。
{燃|も}えるゴミと{燃|も}えないゴミを{分|わ}けてください。
examples.english: Please separate burnable and non-burnable garbage.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{時|とき}に{大量|たいりょう}の{燃|も}えるゴミが{出|で}たので、{何回|なんかい}かに{分|わ}けて{出|だ}した。
examples.english: A large amount of burnable garbage came out during the move, so I put it out in several batches.

notes:
USAGE:
An essential daily-life term in Japan, where garbage is strictly sorted by category. {燃|も}えるゴミ is one of the main categories, along with {燃|も}えないゴミ (non-burnable garbage) and {資源|しげん}ゴミ (recyclable waste). Collection days and sorting rules vary by municipality. Also written as {可燃|かねん}ゴミ on official signs.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {燃|も}えるゴミの{日|ひ} (burnable garbage day)
- {燃|も}えるゴミの{袋|ふくろ} (burnable garbage bag)
- {燃|も}えるゴミに{出|だ}す (to put out as burnable garbage)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {燃|も}えないゴミ: non-burnable garbage — metals, ceramics, glass
- {可燃|かねん}ゴミ: combustible waste — formal equivalent
- {資源|しげん}ゴミ: recyclable waste — paper, cans, bottles, plastics
